subject: Dedicated capacity — measurement suite, SLA guardrails & pricing bands
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@atlasrobotics.com>

Cc: Tom Richards <tom.richards@atlasrobotics.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated commit sizing / measurement expectations

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're getting the procurement deck ready and need to lock down two things before our internal approval: the committed GPU sizing you propose for our copilots workload, and the objective throughput/latency tests Redwood will accept as "evidence" for meeting the SLA in month 1.

Can you share (a) a test plan we can run in our staging account, (b) a short description of the steady-state and cold-start metrics you'll guarantee (tokens/sec, requests/sec, p95 latency), and (c) how discounts map to commit bands? Tom and I will circulate to infra and procurement.

High-level workload notes from our side: mix of short chat completions (~25 tokens average) and longer summarizations (~450 tokens) with a ~15% embedding expansion fanout. Peak 95th percentile concurrency today ~120 concurrent requests; expected 3x growth in 12 months.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Kim
VP Product, Atlas Robotics

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing / measurement expectations

Hi Sara —

Really useful context, thanks. I've attached a compact test plan and a synthetic harness config we'll use for verification. Key summary up front so your infra and procurement can move fast:

- What we guarantee (example band): Sustained 1.2M tokens/sec across the GPU pool for mixed workload A (chat+summaries) with p95 per-request latency <= 320ms for short-chat requests and p95 <= 1.8s for long summaries. Those numbers map to a 5 GPU dedicated pool with our preferred model/quantization profile.
- Measurement methodology: two-phase run — (1) cold-start ramp (30 min) to capture cold-cache and KV priming behaviors, (2) steady-state 2-hour sustained waveform using representative request-size distribution. We report tokens/sec, rps, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and CPU/GPU utilization.
- Pricing/discount structure: baseline reserved commit SKU at $X/hr per GPU. Discounts tiered by 3 commit bands (small/med/large) with additional margin if you accept an industry-standard 7-day rolling overcommit buffer. See attached pricing draft.

I've looped Ben for the commercial model and Laura for onboarding/runbook. If you want we can scope a joint verification window in your staging region — Redwood runs the harness and shares raw logs + summary artifact.

Attached: cap_test_plan_v2.pdf, synthetic_harness_config.yaml, pricing-bands-draft.xlsx

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:51:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing / measurement expectations

Sara / team —

I'll put pricing bands in explicit terms below so procurement has something to bake into the commitment. Numbers are illustrative until we finalize model variant and quantization settings in the run:

- Band A (3-6 GPUs): 8-14% discount off list, baseline SLA tokens/sec as described in Vanessa's note maps to 3 GPUs; throughput scaling linear-ish for our workload until around 12 GPUs where network/persistence becomes dominant.
- Band B (7-16 GPUs): 15-26% discount, priority capacity, can add burst pool at a capped rate.
- Band C (17+ GPUs): 27%+ discount, dedicated control plane options and extended SLOs (4hr incident priority).

Commit mechanics: monthly reserved hours with a 12-month minimum. We can include a one-time headroom credit if test runs show steady-state > committed band during the first 30 days — effectively a performance credit applied to month 2 invoice.

I'll also note two things from ops that Karthik will run through: 1) our synthetic harness includes KV cache priming to avoid optimistic steady-state numbers, and 2) we run a p99 tail-check which must include requests/sec bursts spiking 2.5x for a 5min window. If the system passes both, we sign off on the SLA claim.

Will schedule a short call with your procurement to walk the bands.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing / measurement expectations

Sara — quick technical notes from the verification side so your infra can prepare: 

1) The harness we run is deterministic and config-driven. Provided configs include request-size distribution, concurrency waveform, KV priming cadence, and model checkpoint used. We will provide the exact config we run during the joint window.

2) Measurement buckets we report: total tokens/sec (aggregate), effective rps (successful responses/sec), p50/p95/p99 latencies for both short and long request classes, memory/GPU utilization heatmaps, and the fraction of requests that hit the KV cache vs cold-path.

3) For billing and SLA enforcement the contract will use the 95th-percentile sustained tokens/sec measured over rolling 6-hour windows during the 2-week acceptance period. For month-to-month operations we'll switch to 24-hour rolling windows and use a 95% availability floor.

4) On the GPU sizing note: because of your high ratio of short requests (cheap in tokens but sensitive to per-request latency) we recommend a hybrid pool: 60% of GPUs pinned for low-latency fast-path (smaller batch targets, higher throughput threads), 40% for high-memory long-tail requests (larger batch sizes). That configuration gives better price/performance than a single homogeneous pool for the use case you described.

If you agree I'll export the harness YAML and a small local runner your infra can run to sanity check results before the joint Redwood-run.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sara / Tom —

All good. Short answers:

- We will deliver a redacted performance artifact (raw logs + anonymized traces) and a summary PDF. Redwood's legal team has a standard NDA addendum that covers log sharing; procurement can sign that and we'll proceed.
- Ben and I will assemble a mock invoice showing the discount band and a sample headroom credit applied after the first test run.
- For the joint verification week we only need a staging endpoint and a short-term service account with limited scope (read/write to a staging queue and ability to call the inference endpoint). No VPC peering required for the hosted run; if you prefer private deployment we can discuss the additional network steps.

2) Karthik to share the harness runner and a short sanity-check script (target: 3/11).
3) Sara/Tom to confirm the verification window (target week of 3/15).
